speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) whether the trend of senior re-employment in 2020 and 2021 has been impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic; and (b) if so, what further support can be given to companies to enable them to continue to offer re-employment for their senior employees who are eligible for re-employment.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) how many seniors aged 55 years and above have benefited from the Senior Worker Support Package introduced in 2020; and (b) whether the Government will be looking into extending this support or other ways of promoting senior employability.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Before I start my response, with your permission, Mr Speaker, may I ask the Clerks to distribute a handout on Senior Worker Support Package.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: CPF contribution rates for senior workers aged above 55 to 70 will also be raised by up to two percentage points with effect from 1 January 2022.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The Senior Worker Support Package was introduced in 2020 to support employers in implementing these and other key recommendations made by the Workgroup, and it consists of four schemes.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Members can refer to it in the handout that was just distributed.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: First, the Senior Employment Credit provides employers wage offsets of up to 8% for hiring senior workers aged 55 and above.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: From 1 July 2020 to 31 August 2021, 21,000 senior workers working in 2,800 companies have benefited from the grant.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Thirdly, the Part-time Re-employment Grant supports employers who commit to a part-time re-employment policy whenever eligible senior workers request for it.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: From 1 July 2020 to 31 August 2021, more than 19,000 senior workers working in close to 2,000 companies have benefited from the grant.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: With the healthy take-up rates, the Government topped up over $200 million for both the Senior Worker Early Adopter Grant and the Part-time Re-employment Grant in February this year.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This was on top of $100 million committed to these grants in 2020.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This is comparable to the average of the top three OECD countries.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The re-employment offer rates among eligible private sector resident employees who wished to continue working have also remained high, at well over 90% in 2020.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In addition, last year, the Government introduced the SkillsFuture Mid-Career Support Package to help mature and senior workers stay employable and enter new jobs or new roles.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We have also provided additional support for employers who are expanding local hiring amidst the current economic and labour market uncertainty.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The Jobs Growth Incentive, or JGI, provides wage support to eligible firms that hire new local jobseekers, with higher support for new local hires aged 40 and above, including older workers.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We had recently announced an extension by another six months till March 2022 with tapered support levels, to support employers to continue expanding local hiring.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: JGI-eligible firms that hire mature local hires from October 2021 to March 2022 – the cut-off age is 40 – JGI-eligible firms that continue to hire will receive up to $36,000 per hire.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: With employers continuing to reskill their senior workers and making every effort to retain and hire them, with society supporting their choice to remain active in work, our seniors can continue to participate actively in all spheres of life.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Could I just ask one supplementary question of the Minister?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: While re-employment has stayed steady, is there any data to share whether the kind of roles and the jobs are also similar or have they had to take a cut or part-time employment?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Indeed, the majority of the roles, I can share the exact data later on, but the roles that we have placed in the JGI, the majority of them are in roles that were the same or better – in terms of their draw of the salary levels.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This is the majority of the hires that we placed under the JGI scheme.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: If my memory does not fail me, I think the percentage is more than 60%.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: COVID-19 has been devastating for many families and my residents have told me that in coping with COVID-19, many of them have depleted their intended retirement savings, or that maybe even retrenchments have caused them no choice but to dip into their retirement nest eggs.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: As such, I was very heartened to hear that the Ministry is looking at more training programmes for our seniors, but I would like to ask if there will be more of such training programmes, especially place-and-train programmes for our seniors.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Also, given that most seniors may have to push back the retirement due to the challenges to their livelihoods because of COVID-19, would the Ministry also give us an update on the preparations for the retirement age to be extended to 70 years old, or its plan for the end of the decade?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Some parts of her question, I think I will address in my answer to Question Nos 8 to 16 later.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: For her second Supplementary Question with regard to the planning for retirement, up to 70 years and beyond, we are working closely with MOH in terms of an overall broader construct, in terms of studying how to ensure the healthy ageing, together with healthy productivity, is maintained.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: At this particular point in time, I think it is premature for me to comment.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And they adopted a very dynamic model, but we are still studying it.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: What more can we do to get companies to consider senior employment or get companies to look at job redesign, so that we can hire more of these workers?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: But may I request for your permission to proceed if there are no further supplementary questions on the first two Parliamentary Questions (PQs) filed, so that I can take them all in a more holistic manner with Question Nos 8 to 16.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And if I cannot address in my subsequent answer, then perhaps I could request for the Member to raise the supplementary question again.
